$comment: Config for the loop pipeline (LOOP-ARCHITECTURE.md). Structure only — NEVER secret values. Bootstrapped 2026-07-02; committed 2026-08-12 (previously untracked, so the loops' source of truth existed only in one machine's working tree). Flat shape (no profiles{}) = single-stream repo: the loops run bare with no stream suffix.

git.$worktree_root_note: Set to '..' (sibling-of-checkout) on 2026-09-04, replacing an earlier omission. The prior note reasoned that dropping the key entirely was correct because tzp-3plc/tzp-tiktok also omit it, and that the loops 'resolve worktrees relative to the checkout' — but with the key truly absent, loop-build-v2.md's `<worktree_root>/<name>` template has no defined fallback, and Build improvised a path nested INSIDE the checkout instead of beside it (confirmed: fa-accessible-portal-states/ showed up as an untracked dir in the primary checkout's own git status). tzp-3plc's omission is a different, deliberately-documented special case (shared worktree root across its three profiles, per its own project_tzp_worktree_naming_standard memory), not evidence that omitting is safe here. LOOP-ARCHITECTURE.md's own example configs, kickoff-loops.md's bootstrap fallback (`worktree_root // ".."`), and sibling repos autonomous-site-builder/claude-config all use the literal relative path '..' — this just makes that convention explicit instead of relying on undefined behavior.

ephemeral_recipe.up: createdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432 <db>  (against the always-running `postgresql@17` Homebrew service, brew services list)
ephemeral_recipe.url: postgresql://<user>@127.0.0.1:5432/<db>  (explicit user segment required — helpers.ts's local-host regex won't match a bare postgresql://127.0.0.1:5432/<db>; auth is `trust` locally, no password)
ephemeral_recipe.hostport_strategy: single shared Postgres@17 instance on port 5432; per-item isolation via a uniquely-named DB (createdb/dropdb per round, e.g. fa_build_<ts>), not per-item port allocation

db.note: Updated 2026-09-02 (Bridge) after 3 consecutive Build rounds (52-54) found the `container` binary entirely absent from PATH (not just unreachable — `brew info container` reports "Not installed"), despite the prior apple-container-postgres recipe having been verified working here on 2026-07-02. Cause of the disappearance wasn't chased down; rather than reinstall+reverify an unexplained-missing system dependency, this documents what Build has already been doing successfully for 3+ rounds: local Homebrew postgresql@17 (already running as a background service), createdb/migrate/dropdb per round, genuinely ephemeral, never touches a protected host. If Apple's `container` runtime is reinstalled and confirmed working again on this machine, this block can revert — see git history for the prior apple-container-postgres recipe.

_bootstrap_notes: Status labels mapped from this workspace's custom statuses (no native In-Review/Needs-Info labels existed): review_status=update required, blocked/ambiguous=on hold, done=complete. Chosen unattended on 2026-07-02 with defaults; adjust if wrong. (The build/lint/typecheck/test scripts above were aspirational at bootstrap, pending item 86e24cy2d — that scaffolding has since landed and every command is real and passing as of 2026-08-12.) queue.transport set to "cli" on 2026-08-14 after the MCP ClickUp transport hit a multi-hour rate limit mid-session (several rounds blocked on reads); the `cup` CLI was confirmed reachable and answering the same queries throughout, so every queue operation now goes through `cup` instead of mcp__claude_ai_ClickUp__* tools. merge_policy set to "auto-on-pass-safe" on 2026-08-29 (Principle 4c) after a 30-PR reviewed-pass backlog piled up at the human merge gate with no policy set (absent defaults to "human"); Review's PASS verdict now auto-merges a unit only when every item is S/M appetite, unflagged (no rabbit-hole/solo-risk flag), and CI is fully green — anything else still lands in the manual merge-order table. Added queue.lists.roadmap (901716361915) on 2026-08-31 via Bridge: the configured backlog list (901714899445) was drained (0 at 'to do'), while 57 ready master-scope tasks sat in the unconfigured Roadmap list, invisible to the loop's queue query. Added queue.chat_channel_id (h62ja-746857) on 2026-09-02 at the human's request, via Controller's Step 5 relay resolution (LOOP-ARCHITECTURE-V2.md): confirmed the channel exists and is empty (clickup_get_chat_channel_messages returned 0 messages, no error) via the MCP ClickUp tools, which the chat relay uses regardless of queue.transport=cli (transport only governs task/queue CRUD, not chat). Distinct from the pre-existing 'Freight Audit and Financing' channel (h62ja-483517, matches queue.space_name) — the human gave this specific id explicitly, so it was used as given rather than substituted.
